subject: GlidePath migration: price equivalence ask & packaging details
messages:
From: Aileen Park <aileen@glidepath.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GlidePath exploring replacement — initial price equivalence request

Hi Sofia,

We chatted briefly at the Summit last month — GlidePath is actively evaluating a move off Velocis and your name was recommended by Jamie over on the product team. We have an upcoming renewal (Aug 2025) and a fairly tight procurement window. Before we commit time to a full POC, procurement asked whether Redwood can provide a price-equivalence offering (match current unit economics + limited onboarding credit) and confirm equivalent packaging options (reserved capacity vs consumption + SLA).

Top-level info:
- Current vendor: Velocis — blended effective rate: $0.026/token (usage-heavy embedding workloads + occasional chat).
- Current term: annual commit with a three-month ramp and a 90-day onboarding calendar.
- Key asks: an explicit price-match proposal, targeted onboarding credit to offset migration/e2e testing, and confirmation of SLA and data isolation options for finance/regulatory.

Can you point me to the right contacts and whether a formal price-equivalence offer is possible? Happy to share a short usage export if helpful.

Thanks,
Aileen Park
Senior Product Ops — GlidePath
Aileen: 415-555-0132

Attachment: none in this message
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Aileen Park <aileen@glidepath.io>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 May 2025 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GlidePath exploring replacement — initial price equivalence request

Hi Aileen — great to hear from you, and thanks for the context.

Short answer: yes, we can put together a formal equivalence package. To make it accurate we need a short usage profile (30/90/12mo), a list of critical KPIs (p99 latency SLO, availability, KV cache proportion), and any contractual constraints on data residency. If you can share a CSV with the last 90 days of token-level usage (peak and 95th perc), that will let us calibrate reserved vs consumption mixes.

Preliminary thoughts:
- Two packaging tracks: (A) 12-month reserved commit with onboarding credit; (B) hybrid: lower commit + hosted fallback for burst. We typically match effective run-rate for the first 3 months with a targeted onboarding credit to cover re-instrumentation.
- SLA: we can mirror your current availability target but will need legal to review the exact warranty language.

I attached a quick equivalence checklist that speeds up our internal pricing review — please populate and send back when you can. I’ve looped in Connor (Solutions) to help map the technical fit.

Available to meet next week if you prefer to walk through it. Which timezone are you in?

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

From: Ben Wallace <benw@glidepath.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 May 2025 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GlidePath exploring replacement — initial price equivalence request

Sofia — thanks for the quick reply. Attaching the 90-day usage export and a short RACI. Highlights:
- 90-day avg token/day: 18M (embedding-heavy; 70% batched embeddings, 25% chat short-turns, 5% long-gen).
- Peak: 52M tokens/day on Black Friday spike simulation.
- Current commercial: $0.026/token blended; annual commit w/three-month ramp as Aileen noted.

Procurement/finance are specifically asking for:
1) A price-equivalence term sheet that shows how Redwood would match effective blended unit economics for the first 3 months.
2) Clear onboarding credit (one-time) to offset integration and egress costs.
3) Explicit statement about private deployment / VPC option (they require data isolation).

We’ve attached glidepath-usage-summary.csv. If you can turn that into a draft term sheet + brief run-rate comparison, we can share internally and aim for a procurement call next Tuesday.

Ben Wallace
Head of Commercial Operations — GlidePath

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 May 2025 11:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: GlidePath price-equivalence request (GP-2025-042)

Team — forwarding GlidePath usage and the ask. Summary + proposed structure below, please review and reply with redline/comments. We need a quick paper to send Monday AM.

Summary:
- Customer: GlidePath (high-volume embedding workload; 18M avg tokens/day, big peak potential).
- Objective: Price-match to $0.026/token blended for first 3 months + onboarding credit. They need VPC/private option and an SLA review.

Proposed commercial architecture (initial):
1) Offer A: 12-month Reserved Commit — 45% of their 90-day avg committed upfront for a 12-month term. Effective blended rate target: match $0.026/token for months 0–3 via a one-time onboarding credit (applied as invoice credit over first invoice cycle).
2) Offer B: Hybrid Guardrail — 25% commit + consumption for burst; we provide a migration credit equal to 2 months of expected consumption spend (to offset switching).
3) Operational: Include private deployment option (Redwood Private) under separate SOW. SLA to mirror availability target; legal to scope data residency language.

Risks / ops notes:
- Need to confirm KV-cache impact on token count (Connor) — billing model must account for pre-computed embeddings vs generation tokens.
- Peak spikes will push us into burst capacity frequently; this affects unit economics on a pure reserved model (Karthik).

Attachments: proposed-structure.pdf (stub) — contains a simple P&L and discount ladder.

Ask: Jonas — approve the outline (or propose alternative discount ladder). Karthik — can you run a quick 12-month P&L with the hybrid scenario? Connor — confirm any billing caveats for embedded cache reconciliation. I’ll draft the term sheet once you confirm.

Thanks,
Sofia

Attachment: proposed-structure.pdf (stub)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 May 2025 09:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: GlidePath price-equivalence request (GP-2025-042)

Sofia — quick thumbs up on the proposed structure. Two tactical adjustments I recommend:

1) Discount ladder: Offer a 12% effective discount applied to committed volume for the first 90 days (this plus onboarding credit should get to parity with $0.026/token once we apply our volume tiers). Avoid matching exactly — keep a 5–10% premium in sustained months to protect margin.
2) Onboarding credit: make it performance-tied — 50% on contract signature, 50% after successful data cutover & baseline latency verification. That reduces our one-way risk.

Connor: note the KV cache reconciliation ask. If caching reduces chargeable token count materially, we should have a line-item exception in the term sheet to avoid unexpected revenue leakage.

If legal is OK with the VPC wording we can send a clean term sheet Monday.

Jonas
VP, Commercial — Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Aileen Park <aileen@glidepath.io>, Ben Wallace <benw@glidepath.io>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 May 2025 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood: formal price-equivalence offer (draft term sheet) — GP-2025-042

Hi Aileen / Ben — thanks for the usage export and patience while we reviewed. Attached is a draft term sheet that reflects a price-equivalence path and two packaging options. High level: 

- Option 1 (Reserved): 12-month commit at 45% of 90-day avg; onboarding credit applied as invoice credit to reach effective parity (~$0.026/token) during months 0–3. Discount ladder thereafter (see attached) to transition to our standard rate.
- Option 2 (Hybrid): 25% commit + pay-as-you-go for burst. Migration credit equal to 2x expected month-0 consumption spend to offset egress and integration.
- VPC/private deployment: available; will be scoped in a separate SOW with standard Private deployment fee.
- Onboarding credit is performance-tied (50% on signature, 50% after cutover validation).

Next steps: please review the attached term sheet and confirm if procurement would like a separate SOW for Redwood Private (we can loop legal). If useful, we can schedule a procurement call Tuesday to walk through numbers and finalize SLA wording.

Thanks — look forward to moving this forward.

Best regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199
